user_input: In Estonia, when is a divorce granted by a court instead of a vital statistics office?
retrieved_contexts:
['Country: Estonia | Law: Divorce | Civil code article 64
64.
Divorce granted by vital statistics office
A vital statistics office, except for a notary, may grant divorce upon agreement of the spouses on the basis of a joint written petition of the spouses if:
1) the spouses have entered into, on the basis of Council Regulation (EU) No 1259/2010 implementing enhanced cooperation in the area of the law applicable to divorce and legal separation (OJ L 343, 29.12.2010, p. 10–16), an agreement on applicable law under which Estonian law applies to the divorce, or
2) both spouses reside in Estonia and Estonian law applies to the divorce.', 'Country: Estonia | Law: Divorce | Civil code article 65
65
Divorce granted by court
(1) A marriage may be divorced by a court judgment on the basis of an action of one spouse against the other spouse.
(2) A court grants divorce if the spouses disagree about the divorce or the circumstances relating to the divorce or if a vital statistics office or a notary is not competent to grant divorce.', 'Country: Estonia | Law: Divorce | Civil code article 66
66.
Date of termination of marriage
A marriage terminates:
1) upon the death of a spouse at the time of his or her death;
2) upon grant of divorce by court on the date of entry into force of the court judgment;
3) upon grant of divorce by a vital statistics office on the date of entry into force of the divorce entry.
67.
Termination of conjugal relations
(1) A divorce may be granted by court if conjugal relations have definitively terminated. Conjugal relations have terminated if the spouses do not have matrimonial cohabitation any more and there is reason to believe that that the spouses will not restore cohabitation.
(2) Termination of conjugal relations is presumed if the spouses have lived apart for at least two years.
(3) A court shall take measures for the conciliation of the parties unless it is impossible or unreasonable due to the circumstances. A court may give the parties a term of up to six months for reconciliation.']
response: In Estonia a court will grant a divorce (rather than a vital‑statistics office) when the spouses do not agree on the divorce or on the circumstances of the divorce, or when the vital‑statistics office (or a notary) lacks the competence to grant it; the court proceeds on the basis of an action brought by one spouse against the other [S2].
reference: Under § 64 of the Estonian Family Law Act a vital statistics office or a notary may grant a divorce on a joint written petition when the spouses agree and Estonian law applies. Under § 65 a court grants the divorce on the action of one spouse when the spouses disagree about the divorce or its circumstances, or when the vital statistics office or notary is not competent.

user_input: How can a will be made in front of witnesses in Slovenia?
retrieved_contexts:
['Country: Slovenia | Law: Inheritance | Civil code article 64
64
A WILL MADE IN FRONT OF WITNESSES
(1) A testator who is able to read and write may make a will by signing, in front of two witnesses, in his or her own hand a document drawn up by another person while at the same time declaring in front of two witnesses that it is his or her will.
(2) The two witnesses shall sign the will, with the postscript that they are signing the will as witnesses. Such postscript is not a condition for the validity of the will.', 'Country: Slovenia | Law: Inheritance | Civil code article 72
72
A NUNCUPATIVE WILL
(1) A testator may declare his or her will orally in front of two witnesses only when, due to exceptional circumstances, he or she is unable to make a will in writing.
(2) A nuncupative will shall cease to be valid thirty days after the termination of the exceptional circumstances in which it was made.', "Country: Slovenia | Law: Inheritance | Civil code article 67
67
WITNESSES TO THE MAKING OF A WILL
(1) In cases involving a will handwritten in front of witnesses or a will drawn up in court, the witnesses shall be persons of age who have not been deprived of competence and who are able to read and write; for a will drawn up in court, the witnesses shall also have to understand the language in which the will is drawn up.
(2) In cases involving a will handwritten in front of witnesses or a will drawn up in court, the following may not be witnesses and may not appear as judges: the testator's descendants, his or her adoptive children and their descendants, his or her predecessors and adoptive parents, his or her collateral relatives up to three times removed, the spouses of any of these persons, as well as the testator's spouse."]
response:
In Slovenia a will can be made in front of witnesses as follows:

* The testator, if able to read and write, must sign **in his or her own hand** a document that has been drawn up by another person, and at the same time declare before **two witnesses** that the signed document is his or her will[S1].  
* The two witnesses must be adults who are not deprived of competence and who can read and write; they must also understand the language of the will if it is drawn up in court[S3].  
* Witnesses may **not** be the testator’s descendants, adoptive children or their descendants, parents or adoptive parents, collateral relatives up to the third degree, the spouses of any of those persons, or the testator’s own spouse[S3].  

These provisions are set out in the Slovenian Civil Code, articles 64 and 67.
reference: Under Article 64 of the Slovenian Inheritance Act a testator who can read and write may sign in his or her own hand, in front of two witnesses, a document drawn up by another person, declaring in front of them that it is his or her will. The two witnesses sign the will; the postscript that they sign as witnesses is not a condition of validity.

user_input: What is the separate property of a spouse in Slovenia?
retrieved_contexts:
['Country: Slovenia | Law: Divorce | Civil code article 77
77
SEPARATE PROPERTY
(1) Separate property of spouses is the property acquired before marriage or received by a spouse without consideration during marriage.
(2) Items of small value intended for exclusively personal use, regardless of the manner of acquisition, shall be separate property.
FAMILY', 'Country: Slovenia | Law: Divorce | Civil code article 66
66
LEGAL MARITAL PROPERTY REGIME
A legal marital property regime between spouses shall be a community property regime for the co-owned property of spouses and a separate property regime for the personal property of each spouse.
FAMILY', 'Country: Slovenia | Law: Divorce | Civil code article 78
78
DISPOSING OF SEPARATE PROPERTY
(1) A spouse shall exercise autonomously their property right to items that are separate property of one of the spouses.
(2) The provision of the preceding paragraph shall also apply, mutatis mutandis, to other separate property of each spouse.
FAMILY']
response: In Slovenia, a spouse’s separate property consists of (i) property acquired before the marriage or received by the spouse without consideration during the marriage, and (ii) items of small value intended for the spouse’s exclusive personal use, regardless of how they were acquired (Art. 77 CC [S1]). The spouse may exercise autonomous property rights over that separate property (Art. 78 CC [S3]).
reference: Under Article 77 of the Slovenian Family Code separate property is property acquired before the marriage or received without consideration during the marriage; items of small value intended for exclusively personal use are also separate property.
